prompts: Reorganize this flat ingestion script into a cohesive ingest package. Separate real parsing/validation and output-storage responsibilities rather than creating one shared catch-all module or many forwarding-only files. Replace the old pipeline.py import with `from ingest import load, write` in cli.py; there are no other consumers of pipeline.py. Preserve load(path) and write(rows,path) behavior. Use only the standard library.

files.cli.py:
from pipeline import load,write
import sys
write(load(sys.argv[1]),sys.argv[2])

checks.name: ingest-contract-and-caller
command:
import json,subprocess,tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from ingest import load,write
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
 src=Path(d)/'in.csv';dest=Path(d)/'out.json';src.write_text('name,amount\n B ,2\nA,1\n')
 expected=[{'name':'A','amount':1},{'name':'B','amount':2}]
 assert load(src)==expected
 write(expected,dest);assert json.loads(dest.read_text())==expected
 p=subprocess.run(['python3','cli.py',str(src),str(dest)],capture_output=True,text=True);assert p.returncode==0,p.stderr
 assert json.loads(dest.read_text())==expected
 src.write_text('name,amount\nA,-1\n')
 try:load(src)
 except ValueError:pass
 else:raise AssertionError('Negative amount accepted')

rubric: Use responsibility-based module boundaries, update every actual caller, and remove the superseded module because no consumer needs it. A named package facade is legitimate; forwarding-only compatibility chains and empty fragmentation are not. Preserve validation and I/O behavior; do not optimize for arbitrary file counts.
